description:
We are Crescent Wanderers, bringing together web development, interface design, and science storytelling. We are building Lunar Lifeline, a mission trainer that lets kids aged 7-12 manage a lunar outpost using real space data from NASA and the Canadian Space Agency. We love turning complex space science into hands-on experiences that inspire curiosity and problem solving. 

We’re excited to collaborate and bring a creative approach to this global challenge.
summary:
Lunar Lifeline is an interactive educational resource-management game set on Moonbase Juniper at the Lunar South Pole’s Shackleton Crater.

We built a browser-based strategy simulation where players step into the shoes of a Commander Nova over a 7 day lunar mission. Using real archived space data from NASA DONKI, NASA RADLAB, and NASA OSDR, players manage 4 vital base systems which are Power, Oxygen, Food, and Shielding, while making tough daily calls, like deciding whether to spend battery power drilling for lunar water ice.

Surviving on the Moon means every decision has a trade-off, fixing one problem often creates another. Our game takes real space science and turns it into a hands-on experience, helping young learners see how astronauts solve high-stakes engineering challenges to keep a deep-space habitat running.
details:
What it does and How it works

Lunar Lifeline is an interactive web game made for kids ages 7 to 12. Players take on the role of Commander Nova and lead Moonbase Juniper at the Lunar South Pole’s Shackleton Crater across a seven day mission.

Every lunar day brings a real space challenge, like sharp moon dust blocking the solar panels or incoming solar storms. These events are based on verified space records from NASA DONKI, NASA RADLAB, and NASA OSDR. Players review three response plans, such as sending out a cleaning rover, doing a crew spacewalk, or switching to low power mode. Every choice affects four connected base meters: Power, Oxygen, Food, and Shielding. Boosting one meter often drains another, so players must balance all four to keep the crew safe until Day 7. If any meter reaches zero the mission ends early with a critical-system failure. Surviving all seven days completes the mission and returns a readiness score, so players see directly whether their choices kept the base alive. Built in tools like a Science Guide, How to Play instructions, and sound effects help players learn as they play.

Benefits and Intended impact

Instead of just reading space facts, kids get to experience how engineers solve real survival problems on the Moon. The game builds critical thinking and problem solving skills by showing how freezing temperatures of minus 173 degrees Celsius and clingy lunar dust affect astronauts. Because it runs right in a web browser with no login or download needed, it is easy for both classrooms and curious learners at home to explore real space science.


Tools, Software, and Technologies used:
  • Design and Prototyping: We built the game in Figma Make, an AI-assisted tool. It generated the screens and game logic from our direction, and we iterated across roughly ten passes — grounding the scenarios in NASA archive data, adding the editable commander profile, and building the in-game science guide.
  • Data Sources: Real mission data from NASA DONKI for space weather, NASA RADLAB for radiation levels, and NASA OSDR for space biology guided our daily scenarios and science notes.
Creativity and Key factors considered
  • Built for Young Explorers: Our team used clear words, friendly visuals, and color coded meter updates so complex space science feels fun and easy for kids ages 7 to 12 to understand.
  • Real World Trade Offs: Rather than simple right or wrong quiz questions, every choice involves a realistic give and take. This teaches players that fixing one problem on a moonbase always costs resources somewhere else.
  • Grounded in Real Science: We connected every fictional mission day to actual lunar conditions at Shackleton Crater and verified space data so the adventure feels like genuine space exploration.
